summary.headline: Bank of Baroda Q1 FY27 net profit fell to INR 1,278 crore after a USD 600 million NMC settlement; ex-item profit was INR 5,528 crore.
summary.overview: Global business reached INR 30.5 lakh crore, up 15.4% YoY, with global advances up 17.4% and domestic deposits up 14.7%. Operating profit was INR 8,127 crore, roughly flat YoY, as NII grew 9.5% but treasury income fell to about INR 800-900 crore from over INR 2,000 crore a year earlier. The USD 600 million NMC out-of-court settlement, paid on 1 July 2026 and expensed in Q1, cut reported ROA to 0.25% (1.10% excluding the item). Asset quality improved YoY, with GNPA at 1.99%, credit cost at 0.29% and slippage at 0.91%, though sequentially GNPA and NNPA ticked up due to a lower write-off of INR 625 crore versus INR 2,200 crore a year earlier.

financial_highlights.change: GNPA -29 bps YoY; Net NPA -10 bps YoY

financial_highlights.metric: Domestic CASA ratio / domestic CD ratio

segments.name: Advances
segments.commentary: Global advances +17.4% YoY (domestic +16.1%, international +23.3%). Organic retail +18.4%, agriculture +18.7%, organic MSME +20.3%, corporate +15.3%; auto +25.3%, mortgage +27.4%, home loan +14.7%, education +10.8%.

segments.name: Deposits
segments.commentary: Total deposits +13.8% YoY (domestic +14.7%, international +8.9%). Domestic CASA +10% and term deposits +17.8%; management says current account growth was 14.5%.

segments.name: Treasury and other income
segments.commentary: Treasury income about INR 800-900 crore versus over INR 2,000 crore in Q1 FY26, mainly on revaluation as G-sec yields rose to about 6.78% from about 6.10%. Recoveries from technical write-offs exceeded INR 1,000 crore, and PSLC sales of about INR 270 crore were added. Commission and fee income fell about 47% YoY.

segments.name: International book
segments.commentary: Overseas book is about 16-17% of global book and grew 15-20% over recent quarters; international NIM is about 1.4-1.5%.

guidance_outlook: Credit growth 12-14% (unchanged despite outperformance; management cites geopolitical caution).
NIM 2.75-2.95%; slippage ratio 1-1.25%; credit cost below 0.6%; ROE 15-16%.
Full-year ROA guidance deferred to Q2; management expects Q2-Q4 ROA above 1%, and said full-year ROA may not exceed 1%.

ECL transition impact about INR 12,000 crore (about 110 bps on CRAR), with INR 2,500 crore floating provision offsetting part; run-rate credit cost impact about 15-20 bps (earlier cited 20-22 bps on CRAR).
FCNR(B)/OFCB/ECB inflow target USD 4-5 billion; about USD 600-700 million raised so far; USD 1 billion expected via bonds; swap window open until 31 December.
capex_capacity: Capital plan: INR 8,500 crore equity over the medium term to March 2028; about INR 6,000 crore Tier 2 intended in FY27, subject to pricing and timing.
Branches: about 8,400 total; about 260 added last year. Headcount hiring plan of about 7,000 in FY27 after about 6,000 planned last year.
IT budget (OPEX plus capex) above INR 4,000 crore.
Average LCR about 127%; management targets around 120%.
Investment duration increased QoQ and YoY; yields on the book moved from a peak of about 7.13-7.14% to about 6.75-6.80%.
demand_pricing: Corporate book shows a YTD decline. Management says it let go of some low-priced non-MCLR assets and is moving them to MCLR or near-MCLR, helping asset yields.

Bulk deposits and CD together were about INR 2.31 lakh crore, of which bulk deposits were INR 2.11 lakh crore. Bulk deposit rates eased after the FCNR(B) scheme, so incremental bulk deposit cost is now below March levels, per management.
FCNR(B) Rupee deposit rate of about 6.4-6.5% is the landed cost of funds. Loans against FCNR(B) are offered to NRIs, and overseas branches price these loans at their own cost of funds.
Domestic NIM at 2.93% described as top quartile. Global NIM is also described as top quartile.

qa_highlights.question: Why did the bank settle the NMC case, and what changed from the annual report stance of defending it?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the defence position is unchanged, but the decision reflected the stage of trial and negotiation, legal advice, and time and cost. The settlement was USD 600 million, the terms are confidential, and it was described as far below the oral claim quantum. Recovery against principal individuals continues in India and abroad.

qa_highlights.question: Why was there no specific provision earlier, and what is the ECL transition impact?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said a specific provision is not allowed on litigation under legal advice. The ECL transition impact is about INR 12,000 crore (110 bps CRAR), offset by the INR 2,500 crore floating provision, with the remainder to be amortised. Credit cost impact is about 15-20 bps; CRAR impact per year is about 20-22 bps.

qa_highlights.question: Why not raise the credit growth guidance given strong performance?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited geopolitical headwinds and uncertainty over deposit growth. It said guidance could be upsized if deposit growth becomes more certain.

qa_highlights.question: What drove the decline in treasury and other income?
qa_highlights.answer: Treasury income fell to about INR 800-900 crore from over INR 2,000 crore, mainly due to revaluation as yields moved. This was offset partly by about INR 1,000 crore of TWO recoveries and PSLC sales of about INR 270 crore.

qa_highlights.question: What is the outlook for the NIM and the FCNR(B) inflows?
qa_highlights.answer: Management reaffirmed the 2.75-2.95% NIM guidance, citing asset repricing and lower incremental bulk deposit costs. FCNR(B) inflows are targeted at USD 4-5 billion, with about USD 1 billion expected via bonds, subject to pricing.

qa_highlights.question: Is there stress in the book from global headwinds, and what do the asset quality indicators show?
qa_highlights.answer: No; CRILC SMA-1 and 2 fell to 0.07% from 0.40% a year earlier, and collection efficiency excluding agriculture was 99.2%. Management said ECLGS supports MSMEs and that slippage and recoveries were better YoY.

risks_watch: NMC settlement: the terms are confidential and the case is sub-judice against other defendants; management says no further claims on the bank in the two courts.
ROA: full-year guidance deferred to Q2; management expects Q2-Q4 ROA above 1%, but the Q1 reported figure was 0.25%.
ECL transition: about INR 12,000 crore impact and a 15-20 bps run-rate credit cost increase. Management said pricing pass-through is subject to RBI spread-change rules.
Margin pressure: asset growth of 16-17% is running ahead of NII, with the NIM at 2.77% against 2.8%+ last quarter.
Sequential rise in GNPA and NNPA due to a lower write-off (INR 625 crore) and a lower denominator. Management said write-offs were kept conservative to protect PCR.
Funding and capital: the INR 8,500 crore equity raise (by March 2028) and about INR 6,000 crore Tier 2 are pending; the FCNR(B) and dollar bond timing depend on pricing.
Non-interest income: commission and fee income fell about 47% YoY; management says pricing is under review.
summary.management_tone: Confident on balance sheet growth, asset quality and capital, but defensive on the NMC settlement, which management declined to detail beyond its commercial rationale. Cautious on guidance: credit growth is held at 12-14% and full-year ROA is deferred, citing geopolitics. Some answers were vague (ECL run-rate, pricing pass-through), and the CEO pushed back on the view that the quarter was weak.
key_quotes: The liability of the Bank in these proceedings is limited to the sum of USD 600 million, which was paid on 1st July 2026.
Without the impact of this exceptional item, net profit for the quarter would have been INR 5,528 crores.
The Bank continues to hold the floating provision of INR 2,500 crores.
So, in terms of the Bank's ability to grow, I think, with a large franchisee of almost 8,400 branches

adds.what: About 260 branches added last year (total about 8,400 branches)

growth.why: Management held FY27 credit growth guidance at 12-14% and deposit growth at 10-12% despite global advances up 17.4% YoY; backing is partial, citing branch network, ~7,000 hiring plan, FCNR(B) inflows of USD 4-5 billion target, and repricing of non-MCLR assets, with no specific new capacity numbers beyond branches.
